The gain (1.024) and offset (-0.8 mV) match the resistor values, and power (81 µW) is well under budget. The only failing spec is bandwidth, 112 MHz against a 140 MHz target. Closed-loop bandwidth here is roughly GBW/1.024, so GBW is about 115 MHz and needs to rise to about 143 MHz. That points to the input gm (set by the tail current) or the compensation capacitor. Among those, the tail mirror M5 is the most likely fault, since its W/L ratio against M6 sets the tail current and a reduced tail current lowers gm1 and GBW. I can't confirm the original sizing from the netlist alone, so this is a ranked inference, not a verified result.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "Cc", "M1"], "fault": "Tail current mirror M5 is under-sized (W=2.02 um, L=2.34 um, giving about a 4.1x mirror ratio against M6). The reduced tail current lowers gm1 and therefore the GBW, which drops closed-loop bandwidth to 112 MHz. Restoring the nominal width should bring bandwidth back above 140 MHz."}
```
